title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Cardiac Rhythm Problems in Spaceflight — Cephalad Fluid Shift and Hemodynamics
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Cephalad Fluid Shift and Hemodynamics: Microgravity eliminates hydrostatic pressure gradients, causing an immediate shift of approximately 1.5 to 2 liters of intravascular and interstitial fluid from lower extremities toward the thorax and head. This acute central hypervolemia alters autonomic tone and baroreflex sensitivity.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Cardiac Rhythm Problems in Spaceflight — Autonomic Dysregulation and HRV
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Autonomic Dysregulation and HRV: Prolonged exposure to weightlessness alters sympathetic and parasympathetic balance. Heart rate variability (HRV RMSSD) demonstrates reduced vagal modulation during acute mission adaptation and during heavy EVA operational workloads.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Cardiac Rhythm Problems in Spaceflight — Cardiac Arrhythmias in Flight
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Cardiac Arrhythmias in Flight: Premature ventricular and atrial contractions have been observed in flight telemetry during shuttle and ISS missions. While most ectopy is clinically benign, strenuous extravehicular activity combined with adrenergic surges elevates ectopy incidence.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Cardiac Rhythm Problems in Spaceflight — Post-Flight Orthostatic Intolerance
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Post-Flight Orthostatic Intolerance: Upon return to Earth's 1g or planetary gravity, astronauts frequently experience orthostatic intolerance, marked by postural tachycardia, presyncope, and decreased peripheral vasoconstrictive reserve.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Cardiac Rhythm Problems in Spaceflight — Cardiovascular Countermeasures
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Cardiovascular Countermeasures: Daily high-intensity resistive and aerobic countermeasure protocols on the ARED and T2 cycle ergometer help preserve myocardial mass and peripheral vascular tone throughout long-duration orbital missions.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Cardiac Rhythm Problems in Spaceflight — Resting Vitals Operational Baselines
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Resting Vitals Operational Baselines: Nominal resting heart rate ranges from 55 to 90 bpm. Persistent resting tachycardia exceeding 100 bpm outside exertion warrants medical evaluation for dehydration, thermal stress, cabin hypercapnia, or occult infection.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Cardiac Rhythm Problems in Spaceflight — Myocardial Deconditioning
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Myocardial Deconditioning: Left ventricular mass decreases by roughly 8% to 10% during 6-month orbital flights due to reduced cardiovascular workload in the absence of gravitational hydrostatic pressure.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Hypercapnia and Spaceflight Atmospheric Effects — Spacecraft Atmospheric CO2 Concentration
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Spacecraft Atmospheric CO2 Concentration: Unlike terrestrial ambient levels (approx. 0.3 mmHg / 400 ppm), spacecraft habitat life-support systems historically operate at higher carbon dioxide partial pressures, commonly between 2.0 and 4.0 mmHg.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Hypercapnia and Spaceflight Atmospheric Effects — Absence of Natural Convection
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Absence of Natural Convection: In weightlessness, natural thermal buoyancy is absent. Without active mechanical air circulation, exhaled CO2 accumulates into stagnant micro-pockets around sleeping or stationary crew members, causing localized hypercapnia.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Hypercapnia and Spaceflight Atmospheric Effects — Hypercapnic Headaches and Neuro-ocular Link
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Hypercapnic Headaches and Neuro-ocular Link: Elevations in cabin PCO2 above 2.5 mmHg correlate with increased crew reports of neurovascular headaches, facial fullness, and lethargy. Cerebral vasodilation from CO2 is investigated as a co-factor in Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS).
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Hypercapnia and Spaceflight Atmospheric Effects — Respiratory and Metabolic Response
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Respiratory and Metabolic Response: Compensatory physiological responses to elevated ambient CO2 include mild tachypnea, increased minute ventilation, and gradual renal retention of bicarbonate to buffer respiratory acidosis.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Hypercapnia and Spaceflight Atmospheric Effects — Cabin ECLSS Monitoring Standards
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Cabin ECLSS Monitoring Standards: NASA flight operational targets specify maintaining 24-hour average cabin PCO2 below 2.0 mmHg in crew sleep quarters, with mandatory scrubber re-activation if levels exceed 3.0 mmHg.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Radiation Carcinogenesis and Acute Radiation Syndromes — Deep Space Ionizing Radiation Environment
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Deep Space Ionizing Radiation Environment: Beyond the geomagnetic protection of Low Earth Orbit, crew members are exposed to Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCR) composed of energetic protons and high-Z/high-energy (HZE) nuclei, alongside sporadic Solar Particle Events (SPE).
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Radiation Carcinogenesis and Acute Radiation Syndromes — Galactic Cosmic Rays Characteristics
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Galactic Cosmic Rays Characteristics: GCR produces a chronic, low dose-rate exposure of approximately 1.0 to 1.5 mSv/day during interplanetary transit. HZE particles create dense linear ionization tracks producing complex double-strand DNA breaks.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Radiation Carcinogenesis and Acute Radiation Syndromes — Solar Particle Events and Storm Shelters
section: Solar Particle Events and Storm Shelters
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Solar Particle Events and Storm Shelters: Coronal mass ejections can deliver dangerous proton radiation dose rates (>1000 mGy) within hours. Habitat storm shelter protocols utilize surrounding water walls, food storage, and polyethylene shielding to attenuate proton fluxes.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.
keywords: solar particle events and storm shelters

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Radiation Carcinogenesis and Acute Radiation Syndromes — Acute Radiation Syndrome Prodrome
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Acute Radiation Syndrome Prodrome: Prodromal symptoms of significant acute radiation exposure include anorexia, nausea, fatigue, and subfebrile temperature occurring within hours to days following exposure.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Radiation Carcinogenesis and Acute Radiation Syndromes — Radiation Exposure Limits
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Radiation Exposure Limits: NASA Permissible Exposure Limits (PEL) restrict career radiation exposure to prevent exceeding a 3% risk of exposure-induced death from cancer. Short-term operational limits include 250 mSv within a 30-day window.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Performance Decrements Associated with Sleep Loss and Circadian Desynchronization — Cumulative Sleep Debt in Spaceflight
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Cumulative Sleep Debt in Spaceflight: Astronauts historically sleep an average of 6.0 to 6.4 hours per night in orbit, accumulating significant sleep debt that progressively impairs cognitive vigilance, reaction time, and fine motor precision.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Performance Decrements Associated with Sleep Loss and Circadian Desynchronization — Circadian Desynchrony in Orbit
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Circadian Desynchrony in Orbit: Operating under 16 sunrises and sunsets every 24 hours in LEO blunts endogenous circadian rhythms. Controlled dynamic LED lighting with blue-enriched morning spectra and warm evening spectra supports melatonin synchronization.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Performance Decrements Associated with Sleep Loss and Circadian Desynchronization — Acoustic and Environmental Interference
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Acoustic and Environmental Interference: Continuous environmental noise from ECLSS ventilation fans and pumps (often 55-65 dBA) fragments restorative deep slow-wave sleep in crew compartments.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Performance Decrements Associated with Sleep Loss and Circadian Desynchronization — Psychomotor Vigilance Testing
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Psychomotor Vigilance Testing: The 3-minute Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT) provides an objective measure of behavioral alertness and fatigue-related attention lapses during spaceflight operations.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Risk of Performance Decrements Associated with Sleep Loss and Circadian Desynchronization — Sleep Duration Standards
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Sleep Duration Standards: Operational standards mandate 8 scheduled hours in crew sleeping quarters per 24-hour cycle, with targeted cumulative sleep duration of at least 7.0 hours/night to sustain executive performance.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Nutritional Biochemistry and Glucose Metabolism in Spaceflight — Microgravity Glucose Metabolism Shifts
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Microgravity Glucose Metabolism Shifts: Skeletal muscle unloading in microgravity leads to reduced GLUT4 transporter expression in unloaded postural fibers, predisposing to altered glucose tolerance and subclinical insulin resistance over long missions.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Nutritional Biochemistry and Glucose Metabolism in Spaceflight — Continuous Interstitial Glucose Telemetry
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Continuous Interstitial Glucose Telemetry: Minimally invasive continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) enables tracking of glycemic variability, postprandial responses, and nocturnal excursions under spaceflight nutritional regimens.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Nutritional Biochemistry and Glucose Metabolism in Spaceflight — Stress-Induced Hyperglycemia
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Stress-Induced Hyperglycemia: High-workload operational maneuvers, emergency simulations, and EVA egress trigger sympathetic and cortisol surges, resulting in acute transient stress hyperglycemia.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA Human Research Program Evidence Book: Nutritional Biochemistry and Glucose Metabolism in Spaceflight — Hypoglycemia Operational Hazards
content: [NASA Human Research Program] Hypoglycemia Operational Hazards: Sustained high metabolic output during EVAs (lasting up to 7 hours) combined with delayed meal intake can cause neuroglycopenic hypoglycemia (<70 mg/dL), degrading cognitive focus and manual dexterity.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: Canadian Space Agency: Health Beyond and Clinical Decision Support for Exploration Class Missions — Transition to Autonomous Healthcare
content: [Canadian Space Agency] Transition to Autonomous Healthcare: The CSA Health Beyond initiative focuses on transitioning space healthcare from Earth-dependent real-time telemedicine to autonomous, crew-centered decision support for exploration missions beyond LEO where communications latency precludes real-time consultations.

title: Canadian Space Agency: Health Beyond and Clinical Decision Support for Exploration Class Missions — Communication Latency Realities
content: [Canadian Space Agency] Communication Latency Realities: On lunar missions, comms latency is approximately 1.3 seconds each way. On Mars transit missions, round-trip delay ranges from 8 to 44 minutes, necessitating onboard decision-support algorithms to guide response during acute clinical incidents.
licence_terms: Government of Canada Terms and Conditions / Crown Copyright. Non-commercial personal and public educational reproduction permitted with attribution to CSA. Commercial redistribution requires prior written permission.

title: Canadian Space Agency: Health Beyond and Clinical Decision Support for Exploration Class Missions — Decision Support vs Autonomous Diagnosis
content: [Canadian Space Agency] Decision Support vs Autonomous Diagnosis: Clinical algorithms in exploration class missions provide structured decision support, anomaly identification, and protocol referencing; they do not replace the clinical judgment of human flight surgeons or issue definitive medical diagnoses.

title: Canadian Space Agency: Health Beyond and Clinical Decision Support for Exploration Class Missions — Behavioral Support in Confinement
content: [Canadian Space Agency] Behavioral Support in Confinement: Proactive behavioral monitoring, mood tracking, and asynchronous communication countermeasures mitigate the psychological stresses of isolation and physical confinement during multi-month exploration voyages.

title: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1: Crew Health and Medical Operations — Medical Authority and Operational Command
content: [NASA] Medical Authority and Operational Command: The Flight Surgeon holds operational medical authority for crew health and mission go/no-go recommendations. The onboard Crew Medical Officer (CMO) administers clinical care under ground guidance or approved autonomous protocols.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1: Crew Health and Medical Operations — Vital Signs Monitoring Standards
content: [NASA] Vital Signs Monitoring Standards: Standards define mandatory clinical monitoring parameters including heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, and core body temperature during acute illness or hazardous mission operations.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1: Crew Health and Medical Operations — Core Temperature Norms
content: [NASA] Core Temperature Norms: Core body temperature standards define normothermia between 36.2 and 37.5 degC. Temperature readings above 38.0 degC indicate fever requiring diagnostic workup, while readings below 35.5 degC require active thermal stabilization.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1: Crew Health and Medical Operations — Blood Pressure Standards
content: [NASA] Blood Pressure Standards: Resting blood pressure exceeding 140/90 mmHg requires serial confirmation, review of sodium and fluid balance, and ground surgeon notification. Systolic pressure below 90 mmHg with dizziness suggests hypovolemia.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 2: Habitability and Environmental Health — Atmospheric Composition and Pressure
content: [NASA] Atmospheric Composition and Pressure: Spacecraft atmospheric total pressure is maintained between 14.7 psi and 8.2 psi depending on exploration phase, with oxygen concentration between 19.5% and 34% by volume.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 2: Habitability and Environmental Health — Carbon Dioxide Limits in Crew Quarters
section: Carbon Dioxide Limits in Crew Quarters
content: [NASA] Carbon Dioxide Limits in Crew Quarters: Partial pressure of carbon dioxide in private crew sleeping quarters must not exceed 2.0 mmHg (0.27 kPa) average over 24 hours to prevent hypercapnic headaches and sleep disturbance.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.
keywords: carbon dioxide limits in crew quarters

title: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 2: Habitability and Environmental Health — Habitable Volume Ventilation Standards
content: [NASA] Habitable Volume Ventilation Standards: Ventilation airflow velocity within habitable volumes shall be maintained between 0.08 m/s (15 ft/min) and 0.20 m/s (40 ft/min) to prevent localized pockets of CO2 and maintain effective atmospheric mixing.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.

title: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 2: Habitability and Environmental Health — Acoustic Exposure Limits in Sleep Quarters
section: Acoustic Exposure Limits in Sleep Quarters
content: [NASA] Acoustic Exposure Limits in Sleep Quarters: Continuous acoustic background noise levels within crew sleep compartments shall not exceed NC-40 (approx. 48 dBA) to ensure restorative sleep and prevent hearing threshold shifts.
licence_terms: Public Domain (U.S. Government Work, 17 U.S.C. § 105). Non-exclusive open distribution.
keywords: acoustic exposure limits in sleep quarters
